title: Padded shape and expanded read
prompt: Your compiler has to work out shapes and reads like these for every movement op. Write pad_shape(shape: list[int], pads: list[int]) -> list[int], the shape of pad x [l0 r0 l1 r1 ...] when x has shape shape. Then write expand_src(shape: list[int], idx: list[int]) -> list[int], the index into x that output index idx reads after an expand of an x with shape shape. Each starter returns one of its arguments unchanged.
hints: pads holds two numbers per axis. Axis k uses pads[2 * k] and pads[2 * k + 1].
pad_shape is one list comprehension: [d + pads[2 * k] + pads[2 * k + 1] for k, d in enumerate(shape)].
expand_src walks both lists together: [0 if d == 1 else i for d, i in zip(shape, idx)].
explain: pad_shape adds each axis's two pad amounts to its size, so [2, 2] with [0, 1, 2, 0] is [3, 4]. expand_src reads every size-1 axis at 0 and leaves the other axes alone, so in a (3, 1) value expanded to (3, 4), output [2][3] reads x[2][0].
